evidence.role: Direct retrieval is grounded in the verified Lesson 7 handoff and controlled definitions

hints: For precision, compare repeated values with one another.
For accuracy, compare a measured value with truth.

walkthrough.text: Precision describes agreement among repeated measurements and is indicated by spread or range.
Accuracy describes closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity.
Keep the comparisons distinct: repeats for precision and truth for accuracy.

ai_rubric.observable: States that precision is the degree of agreement among repeated measurements, indicated by their spread or range
States that accuracy is the closeness of a measured value to the true value of the quantity

evidence.role: Grounds conversion of an absolute measurement uncertainty to a percentage contribution

hints: Divide the absolute uncertainty by the measured value.
Multiply the resulting fraction by 100 percent.

walkthrough.text: Fractional uncertainty = 0.3 cm / 6.0 cm = 0.05.
Percentage uncertainty = 0.05 × 100 percent = 5 percent.
Select C.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects 5 percent from (0.3 / 6.0) × 100 percent

evidence.role: Grounds addition of percentage contributions for multiplied measurements

hints: P is a product of two independently measured quantities.
Use the product rule for percentage uncertainties.

walkthrough.text: For P = xy, both relative measurement changes affect P.
Add the percentage uncertainties: 2 percent + 3 percent = 5 percent.
Select C.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects 5 percent by adding the 2 percent and 3 percent contributions for a product

evidence.role: Grounds weighting a percentage uncertainty by the magnitude of a power

hints: The squared x contributes twice.
The denominator contribution is added when assessing uncertainty size.

walkthrough.text: The x squared contribution is 2 × 1.5 percent = 3.0 percent.
The y contribution is 2.0 percent, even though y is in the denominator.
Total = 3.0 percent + 2.0 percent = 5.0 percent, so select C.

ai_rubric.observable: Selects 5.0 percent from 2 × 1.5 percent + 2.0 percent

evidence.role: Grounds conversion between percentage and absolute uncertainty; the additive rod context is original

hints: Add central lengths separately from their absolute uncertainties.
Divide the final absolute uncertainty by the final length.

walkthrough.text: Add the measured lengths to obtain the central total.
Because the relation is a sum, add absolute uncertainties in centimetres.
Divide the combined absolute uncertainty by the total, then multiply by 100 percent.

evidence.role: Grounds determining a final absolute uncertainty

hints: Add the two central lengths.
For an addition, add absolute uncertainties in the common unit.

walkthrough.text: Quote L = (21.1 ± 0.3) cm.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the total length as 21.1 cm
Adds the absolute uncertainties to obtain 0.3 cm and quotes L as (21.1 ± 0.3) cm

evidence.role: Grounds conversion between fractional, percentage and absolute uncertainty

hints: Use 0.3 cm as the numerator and 21.1 cm as the denominator.
Multiply the fraction by 100 percent.

walkthrough.text: Fractional uncertainty = 0.3 / 21.1 = 0.014218..., because the centimetre units cancel.
Percentage uncertainty = 0.014218... × 100 percent = 1.4218... percent.
Report 0.0142 and 1.42 percent to suitable precision.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the fractional uncertainty as 0.3 / 21.1 = 0.0142
Converts the fractional uncertainty to a percentage uncertainty of 1.42 percent

evidence.role: Grounds a multi-measurement quotient, percentage propagation and conversion to absolute uncertainty

hints: Calculate the central result before propagating uncertainty.
For the quotient, add all three fractional contributions.

walkthrough.text: Evaluate S from the supplied relation and retain g cm⁻².
Convert every absolute input uncertainty to a percentage.
Add the three percentage contributions and convert the total back to an absolute uncertainty in S.
Compare the three individual contributions to identify the largest.

evidence.role: Preserves the whole-question pattern of calculating a derived central value before its uncertainty

hints: Multiply l by w before dividing m by the product.
Derive the unit from g divided by cm squared.

walkthrough.text: The magnitude and unit agree with the supplied quotient.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes the measured mass, length and width into S = m / (lw)
Obtains S = 1.40 g cm⁻² with the correct unit

evidence.role: Directly grounds adding percentage contributions across a product and quotient

hints: Find each percentage separately using absolute uncertainty divided by measured value.
All three measurements appear to power one.

walkthrough.text: Mass contributes (0.5 / 84.0) × 100 percent = 0.595 percent.
Length contributes (0.1 / 12.0) × 100 percent = 0.833 percent, and width contributes (0.05 / 5.00) × 100 percent = 1.00 percent.
Add the three contributions: 0.595 percent + 0.833 percent + 1.00 percent = 2.428 percent, or 2.43 percent.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the mass percentage uncertainty as 0.595 percent
Calculates the length and width percentage uncertainties as 0.833 percent and 1.00 percent
Adds all three contributions to obtain a percentage uncertainty in S of 2.43 percent

evidence.role: Grounds turning a combined percentage into a final absolute uncertainty

hints: Write 2.43 percent as 0.0243.
Multiply this fraction by 1.40 g cm⁻².

walkthrough.text: Use the unrounded fraction 0.0242857 with S = 1.40 g cm⁻².
Round consistently and quote S = (1.40 ± 0.03) g cm⁻².
Check that 0.0340 / 1.40 × 100 percent = 2.43 percent.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the absolute uncertainty as 0.0243 × 1.40 = 0.0340 g cm⁻²
Quotes S as (1.40 ± 0.03) g cm⁻² with matching decimal places

evidence.role: Directly grounds comparing derived results through overlap of their uncertainty intervals

hints: Find the lower and upper bound of each result.
Look for any shared values between the intervals.

walkthrough.text: Using the reported first uncertainty gives an interval from 1.37 to 1.43 g cm⁻².
The second interval is 1.44 - 0.04 to 1.44 + 0.04, or 1.40 to 1.48 g cm⁻².
The intervals overlap from 1.40 to 1.43 g cm⁻², so the two results could be consistent.

ai_rubric.observable: Concludes that the two results could be consistent because their uncertainty intervals overlap

evidence.role: Grounds power-weighted percentage propagation and final absolute uncertainty; earlier Module 2 supplies prefix conversion

hints: Convert centimetres and milliseconds to SI units before calculating R.
Use powers three and two when combining percentage uncertainties.

walkthrough.text: Convert both measured values to SI units using earlier prefix knowledge.
Evaluate the supplied relation with k exact.
Calculate input percentages, apply their powers and add the contributions.
Convert the combined percentage to an absolute uncertainty and quote the final result.

evidence.role: Whole-question context grounds converting supplied measurements before a derived calculation

hints: Centi means 10 to the power minus two.
Milli means 10 to the power minus three.

walkthrough.text: The significant figures are unchanged by exact prefix conversions.

ai_rubric.observable: Converts 4.80 cm to 0.0480 m
Converts 2.40 ms to 0.00240 s

evidence.role: Whole-question context grounds computing a central value before propagation

hints: Use the SI values from part (a).
Cube L and square t before dividing.

walkthrough.text: The numerator is 2.21184 × 10⁻⁶ and the denominator is 5.76 × 10⁻⁶.

ai_rubric.observable: Substitutes the SI values into R = kL³ / t²
Obtains R = 0.384 W

hints: Prefix conversion does not change a fractional uncertainty.
Multiply the L contribution by three and the t contribution by two.

walkthrough.text: Percentage uncertainty in L = 0.06 / 4.80 × 100 percent = 1.25 percent.
Percentage uncertainty in t = 0.03 / 2.40 × 100 percent = 1.25 percent.
Total = 3(1.25 percent) + 2(1.25 percent) = 6.25 percent.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates each input percentage uncertainty as 1.25 percent and applies factors 3 and 2 for L³ and t²
Adds the power-weighted contributions to obtain 6.25 percent

evidence.role: Directly grounds converting a percentage uncertainty to an absolute uncertainty

hints: Convert 6.25 percent to 0.0625.
Multiply by the central value 0.384 W.

walkthrough.text: Quote R = (0.384 ± 0.024) W with matching decimal places.
Independent check: 0.0240 / 0.384 × 100 percent = 6.25 percent.

ai_rubric.observable: Calculates the absolute uncertainty as 0.0625 × 0.384 W = 0.0240 W
Quotes the result as R = (0.384 ± 0.024) W, or an accepted consistently rounded equivalent

quality_audit.originality: All learner contexts, numerical values and the planned figure are original. No official wording, data or diagram layout is reproduced.
quality_audit.scope: The lesson teaches only absolute, fractional and percentage uncertainty and their simple propagation through sums, differences, products, quotients and powers.
quality_audit.evidence: All eight mapped P2 leaves and all five complete source-question contexts were reviewed. They ground percentage contributions, powers, absolute uncertainty, range comparison and linked central-value calculations. P1 evidence is deferred and was not inferred.
later_knowledge_excluded: later-topic physical principles from mixed evidence contexts
